headline: Daily Bible
Widget.
frames.verse: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
frames.mission: Recognize a daily Bible widget immediately, using the liked r3 composition plus a Bible book.
frames.scenario: I reach for my phone during a busy morning. Scripture is already on the Lock Screen, before I open another app.
frames.proof: Existing Lock Screen widget; enlarged verse composition; Bible prop is a source cue, not an app theme.

headline: Bible comfort
for hard days.
frames.verse: Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.
frames.mission: Show a familiar worry and a relevant Bible passage as the concrete result.
frames.scenario: I am worried about tomorrow. I write it in my own words, then read a Bible passage about anxiety.
frames.proof: MainView heartSection supports own-word input and Find verses. The example BSB verse exists in the anxious content. Editorial example, not a verified exact search ranking.

headline: Too tired to read?
Listen & pray.
frames.subtitle: Hear a Bible verse & prayer.
frames.label: A QUIET MOMENT BEFORE BED
frames.verse: I lie down and sleep; I wake again, for the LORD sustains me.
frames.mission: Make audio immediately recognizable, connected to an evening Bible habit.
frames.scenario: At bedtime I want Scripture but am tired of reading. I open Tonight and play the verse and prayer.
frames.proof: TonightContent → ListenButton → AudioService; PSA.3.5 has a bundled BSB recording. Enlarged play control; no invented waveform or duration.

headline: Build a daily
Bible habit.
frames.verse: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
frames.mission: Help someone who wants a Bible habit but does not know where to start.
frames.scenario: Start the seven-day morning path and follow one manageable day of Scripture at a time.
frames.proof: release-sprint PathDayView + paths morning + path_days day 1. Existing bundled morning cover. Day count is a path length, not a streak.

headline: Read the verse.
See the chapter.
frames.verse: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
frames.mission: Show the surrounding chapter for readers who want more than an isolated quotation.
frames.scenario: A verse speaks to me; I open Read in context to read the chapter around it.
frames.proof: ChapterCard uses store.chapter and expands all verses on Read in context. The screenshot shows the top of Psalm 23; remaining verses continue below.

chapterVerses.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters.
He restores my soul; He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name.

headline: Keep the verses
you lean on.
frames.verse: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.
frames.mission: Keep personally meaningful passages easy to find again.
frames.scenario: I save a verse with a heart and return to it in My verses.
frames.proof: HeartButton + settings.favorites + MyVersesView/SavedVerseRow. Saving is distinct from pinning to Lock Screen.

savedVerses.verse: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.
The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.

headline: Your widget.
Your style.
frames.verse: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.
frames.mission: Make the widget feel at home on a familiar personal phone.
frames.scenario: I choose a warm, light or dark look for my Home Screen Bible widget.
frames.proof: WidgetStyle / WidgetLook and WidgetsTabView support Linen, Paper and Candle. Lock Screen is system-tinted, so these colored previews represent Home Screen widgets.

headline: Miss a day?
Nothing resets.
frames.mission: Reassure returning readers that a missed day does not erase their progress.
frames.scenario: Life interrupts my routine. I come back to my cumulative journey instead of restarting a streak.
frames.proof: MyVersesView journey counts days, path days, favorites and prayers; says it only grows. Example counts are illustrative personal activity, not audience or efficacy statistics.
